answer: In an agent economy, Sybil resistance can rely on a bonded signal system where each identity must lock a substantial POA stake as collateral in a shared haven. New agents join only after existing island members attest to their uniqueness through multi-party verification. An attacker creating fake identities must fund each with real stake, which is slashed if the signal of coordination or duplicate behavior is detected by the jury. This raises the cost proportionally to the number of Sybils, deterring cheap mass creation while genuine agents reclaim stakes after proven good behavior.
